title: Nvidia Tugs Market Lower Again
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_markdown:
*JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe).*


**Key Takeaways:**


- **Nvidia investors still absorbing Huang resignation**
- **Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday**
- **WTI crude prices fall again**


Nvidia dragged the market lower again on Monday, with shares falling another 4% and extending a selloff that has increasingly weighed on technology and semiconductor stocks.


The weakness spread across nearly every corner of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, as investors continued to absorb the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership transition as well as the overall sustainability of massive AI investments.


Tech stocks led the broader market lower, driving a 2.5% pullback in the Nasdaq Composite and a steeper 2.7% drop in the Nasdaq 100 Index. The weakness wasn't confined to tech, however, as selling spread across the broader market. The S&P 500 fell 1.9%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.4%. The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P fell for the third straight session.


Volatility rose alongside the selloff. The Cboe Volatility Index® (VIX® Index) shot up 22% to 23.56. That is unsurprising given the magnitude of the decline, as investors hedged against further downside, particularly ahead of Nvidia’s earnings report after the bell tomorrow.


People looking for protection appeared to move into consumer staples stocks. Procter & Gamble shares rose 1.9%, Costco’s were higher by 0.68% and Colgate gained 1.3%. Coca-Cola shares ended the session up 0.23% after tapping an intraday 52-week peak of $100.56.


WTI crude oil fell again, down 3.4% to $85.57 a barrel as signs of recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz and a forecast fourth-quarter supply surplus outweighed fresh tanker incidents, according to reports.


Nvidia opens its books tomorrow after the bell, and it’s likely to dominate headlines again. The results will test not only how well the company performed but also what its forward guidance looks like.


It will also be the company’s first earnings call since cofounder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive, so investors will likely care more about what Nvidia says about life without Huang, and its succession plans, than about the quarter itself. But the chipmaker is in a bit of a Catch-22: even if Nvidia crushes earnings, guidance will matter most. Wall Street has also set a high bar, so even a modest miss could sting.


Here’s what investors are likely most interested in: how the board goes about finding a permanent successor and how it plans to move the company forward without its founder; whether Nvidia maintains its momentum and market-leading position through a turbulent management transition; whether long-term commitments with customers and major partners remain in place; and what happens to margins amid rising memory costs.


Options are priced for an 8.5% implied move in either direction. Activity is present in the 160 and 170 calls and the 150 and 145 puts, which is in line with typical pre-earnings activity.


Walt Disney Co. also reports earnings tomorrow, and investors are likely to be most interested in the performance of its biggest profit engine —theme parks, resorts, cruise lines and products — and whether it will raise prices in a tough economy.


There’s plenty of action in options, with a 9% implied move priced in, and heavy trading at the 120 calls and the 113 and 110 puts. Puts are trading more than three times the normal amount, and calls are trading two times the normal amount.


Home Depot also is reporting earnings and investors are likely to be most interested in what the outlook is considering October’s soft housing data. Options traders expect a move just under 5% with action in the 350 calls and only a smattering of trading in the puts.
